summary: Hrishikesh Terdalkar works in computational linguistics and Indology, earning a PhD at IIT Kanpur under Arnab Bhattacharya. He has held positions at IIT Kanpur, Claude Bernard University Lyon 1, BITS Pilani, and IIIT Hyderabad.

Hsiang-Kuang Chou specialized in Sinology and Buddhist studies, studying under Swami Shivananda. In 1960, he was Chancellor of Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy, Professor of Chinese at the University of Allahabad, and a lecturer at the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy.

Hsiao-Lan Hu worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy, earning a PhD from Temple University. In 2017, Hu was attested as an associate professor of Religious Studies and Women's and Gender Studies at the University of Detroit Mercy.

Hsing Yun (1927–2023) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied under teachers including Yinshun, Zhikai, and Ruoshun. He founded Fo Guang Shan and University of the West, serving as abbot of Fo Guang Shan (~1967–1985).
Hsiu-hui Ji is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).

Hsu Yun (1840–1959) was a Buddhist master who studied under Changkai, Miaolian, and Yaocheng. He founded the Buddhist Association of China in 1953, serving as its honorary chairman, and taught numerous students including Hsuan Hua.

Hsu-feng Lee specializes in Buddhist studies. Lee earned a master's degree at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies under Huimin and a PhD from the University of Sydney under Mark Allon (attested 2017).

Hsuan Hua (1918–1995) was a Buddhist master who studied under Chang Zhi and Hsu Yun. He founded the Buddhist Text Translation Society, Dharma Realm Buddhist University, and the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, where he served as abbot (~1976–1995).
Hsueh-li Cheng is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Ohio University (~1973–1974) and the University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo (~1975–2015).

Hu Shih (1891–1962) was a philosopher and Sinologist who studied at Cornell and Columbia under John Dewey. He served as chancellor of Peking University (1946–1948) and president of Academia Sinica (1957–1962).

Huabei Tan specializes in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Tan pursued a PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the supervision of Medawachchiye Dhammajothi (attested 2026).

Huai-Chin Nan (1918–2012) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology, studying under Huanxian Yuan. He taught at the Republic of China Military Academy, served as Professor of Philosophy at Chinese Culture University (~1963–1975), and founded Taihu Great Learning Center.

Huaiyu Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology who studied at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong and completed a doctorate under Stephen F. Teiser. In 2007, he became assistant professor at Arizona State University.

Huaiyuan Yu works in Tibetology and religious studies, having completed a Bachelor of Laws at Xiamen University and an MSc at University College London. In 2023, Yu was a PhD candidate at Xiamen University.

Huanhuan He works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, studying at UCLA (2009–2013). He has held positions at Zhejiang University, Sun Yat-sen University (2017–2026), and the University of Macau (2026).
Huawen Bai (1930–2021) was a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University (~1951–1955) and later served as a professor there (~1955–1996).

Hubert Decleer (1940–2021) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying Buddhist Chinese at KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte. He served as academic director (1987) and senior faculty advisor (1999) at the SIT Graduate Institute.

Hubert Durt (1936–2018) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied under Étienne Lamotte. He served as professor at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, director of the Hobogirin Institute, and professor at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Hugh B. Urban is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (~1993–1998) under Wendy Doniger. Around 1998, he became an associate professor at Ohio State University.
Hugh Canning (d. 1927) worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned an M.A. from Trinity College, Hartford (1910) and became its Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology in 1914.
